items.title: Marian McPartland interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, April 26, 1997
items.q: this drummer named Jimmy Cappers kept saying, “why don’t you play free — why don’t you play free things?”

ctx.x: No, I think I was pretty much doing that kind of thing because I had Michael Moore with me, who was very much into, like he wrote several of those tunes. It’s funny, after a while Michael Moore became very conservative and I always felt bad because it seemed like he led me into this and every time somebody’s around that it’s going to be a little free – I’ll fall back in. I mean I can’t really do it by myself. I’m trying to think exactly when it happened. I think I was playing a place called The Apartment, it was…

made “Ambiance” anyway, and before I had Michael Moore. And this drummer named Jimmy Cappers kept saying, “why don’t you play free — why don’t you play free things?” And I really couldn’t sort of quite understand what it was I had to do, and I kept trying and I’d always end up in a triad or something. And finally I was able to do that very thing. I mean I can do it. But at that time I probably never would have thought of doing “Piano Jazz” with Cecil Taylor. But it’s funny now I love doing that. But I don’t know…

It’s almost as if you have to force yourself to forget some of the things that you have relied on in the past, to see if things come out somewhat by accident. I don’t know. I’ve never been able to do it myself.
